stem:
Kavya holds a polished brass nameplate and a wooden toy coated with shiny wax up to the light.

Which claims correctly judge lustre and whether shine proves a metal? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The polished brass nameplate has a lustrous appearance.
The shiny wax-coated wooden toy is not a metal just because it shines.
The shiny wax-coated wooden toy must be a metal because it shines.
The polished brass nameplate is non-lustrous because brass is not plastic.

teacher.key_rationale: Polished brass is lustrous and usually metallic. Shine alone does not prove a wax-coated wooden toy is a metal. Calling brass non-lustrous because it is not plastic misuses the idea.
